stories.headline: Akhil Gogoi Announces Indefinite Agitation Over Pending Assam Flood Relief
stories.title: Akhil Gogoi Announces Indefinite Agitation Over Pending Assam Flood Relief
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: Raijor Dal president and Sivasagar MLA Akhil Gogoi has announced an indefinite statewide agitation from 2nd October, alleging that the Assam government has failed to meet its 1st October deadline for disbursing flood relief to affected families.
Gogoi said the agitation would begin on Gandhi Jayanti and continue until the government fulfils its commitments to flood victims.

His announcement came after a public rally at Chachal Dharna Ground in Guwahati on 23rd September, where protesters demanded immediate financial assistance and long-term compensation for families affected by the floods.
According to Gogoi, between 30 and 40 per cent of flood-affected families in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat are yet to receive the promised Rs 15,000 interim assistance.
Gogoi is also demanding Rs 10 lakh compensation for each family that suffered major losses in the floods across the four districts.
In a letter to Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, he highlighted families who, he claimed, remain displaced without adequate financial assistance.
The state government has yet to respond to his latest allegations regarding pending payments.

stories.headline: Bank's Fear That Borrower May Flee Country Can't Alone Justify LOC In Perpetuity: Delhi High Court
stories.title: Bank's Fear That Borrower May Flee Country Can't Alone Justify LOC In Perpetuity: Delhi High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court has held that a bank's apprehension that a borrower may flee the country or that its financial claim may be jeopardised cannot, by itself, justify the indefinite continuation of a Look Out Circular (LOC).

Justice Amit Mahajan made the observation while quashing an LOC issued against one Rajat Gupta at the instance of Bank of Baroda in connection with a criminal case arising from loan accounts classified as non-performing assets and subsequently declared fraudulent.

“In the above context, the apprehension expressed by the Bank that the Petitioner may flee the country or financial claim of the Bank cannot be the sole reason to warrant continuation of an LOC in perpetuity, that too when the LOC issued at the instance of CBI has already been suspended,” the Court observed.
The Court noted that the investigation was completed and the CBI had filed four chargesheets, on which the trial court had taken cognisance.

It further observed that Gupta's travel was already subject to the supervision of the trial court, which had granted him bail with conditions, including the requirement to seek permission before travelling abroad.
Gupta, a former director of Govardhan Industries Pvt.
Ltd., had approached the Court seeking quashing of the LOC issued at the instance of the bank.
He submitted that he was engaged in the business of Ayurvedic medicines and needed to travel to Kazakhstan for business purposes.
Despite his requests, the bank had not withdrawn or suspended the LOC.
The Court noted that Gupta had previously been granted permission to travel abroad and had not misused the liberty granted to him.

Holding that an LOC is a coercive measure that cannot be issued or continued routinely merely because a person is facing trial, the Court observed that no material was placed before it to demonstrate that Gupta was likely to abscond.
The Court accordingly quashed the LOC issued at the instance of Bank of Baroda, observing that the LOC issued at the instance of CBI already stood suspended.

stories.headline: Two including, Mohan Limbikai, file nominations for election to Karnataka West Graduates’ constituency
stories.title: Two including, Mohan Limbikai, file nominations for election to Karnataka West Graduates’ constituency
stories.summary: Two candidates, including Congress nominee and former MLC Mohan Limbikai, filed their nomination papers for the election to Karnataka West Graduates’ Constituency of Karnataka Legislative Council in Dharwad on Thursday
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Two candidates, including Congress nominee and former MLC Mohan Limbikai, filed their nomination papers for the election to Karnataka West Graduates’ Constituency of Karnataka Legislative Council in Dharwad on Thursday.
In a release issued here, Deputy Commissioner of Dharwad and Assistant Returning Officer Snehal R. said that two nominations were received on Thursday.
The two nominations were filed by Mallikarjun Gangadhar of Dharwad district, representing the Kittur Kalyana Karnataka Sene, and Mohan Limbikai of Hubballi, representing the Indian National Congress.
On Wednesday, Shivakumar Talawar from Haveri filed two sets of nomination papers, one as independent and another as candidate of Janata Chalavali Bharat Paksha.

Speaking to reporters after filing his nomination papers, Mr. Limbikai said that he would again be filing another set of nomination papers on October 5 along with senior Congress leaders and Ministers.
Mr. Limbikai said that all the eighteen legislators of four districts, along with district in-charge Ministers, would be visiting Dharwad on October 5 to take part in the nomination filing process.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar was expected to participate, he said.
The former MLC said that the graduate voters would favour Congress party as the Congress government had given five guarantee schemes and had initiated recruitment process for filling up 74,000 posts.
Teachers recruitment was also under way and naturally the voters would favour the Congress party, he said.

stories.headline: No bar on conducting byelection in Perundurai, Election Commission tells Madras High Court
stories.title: No bar on conducting byelection in Perundurai, Election Commission tells Madras High Court
stories.summary: It, however, adds that bypolls to Tiruchi East, Ambasamudram, Viralimalai and Karur will have to wait till disposal of connected election petitions
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The legal bar for conduct of byelections in Perundurai Assembly constituency has ended due to the rejection of an election petition related to that constituency on September 8, 2026, the Election Commission of India (EC) has submitted before the Madras High Court.

In its written submissions filed in response to a public interest litigation petition pending before Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan, the EC said the Perundurai bypoll could be conducted before November 24, 2026 if the Supreme Court does not grant any stay.

The EC said the conduct of bypoll would also be subject to the Chief Justice’s Bench exempting Perundurai from an interim order passed by it on July 10, 2026 restraining the commission from notifying bypolls to five vacant constituencies with respect to which election petitions were pending in the High Court.

In so far as the other four constituencies -- Tiruchi East, Ambasamudram, Viralimalai and Karur -- were concerned, the EC said the byelections cannot be notified to them until the election petitions, filed along with a plea to declare either those petitioners or other candidates as returned candidates, were decided.

Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, who had vacated Tiruchi East and retained Perambur after winning from both the seats in the general elections, had contended that he resigned even before the filing of an election petition by DMK candidate S. Inigo Irudayaraj, the EC said the timing of the resignation was immaterial.

The Commission said it would not matter whether an election petition was filed either before or after the resignation because either way a constituency might end up facing an anomalous situation of being represented by two individuals if someone else gets declared as returned candidate by the election tribunal (High Court) after the conduct of bypolls.

Claiming that the deferment of bypolls was “neither indefinite nor indiscriminate,” the EC said the bar would come to an end immediately after the election tribunal disposes of a plea made along with an election petition to declare either the petitioner or some other candidate as returned candidate.

“This has already happened for Perundurai constituency,” the Commission said, and underlined that Section 86(7) of the Representation of People Act, 1951 requires every election petition to be disposed of as expeditiously as possible with an endeavour to conclude the trial within six months.
“The Commission fully recognises the importance of every constituency being represented...
The Commission would welcome any direction this court considers appropriate for the expeditious disposal ofthe pending election petitions,” the EC’s written submissions read.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Judges Not Meeting 'One Nation One Election' Committee
stories.title: Supreme Court Judges Not Meeting 'One Nation One Election' Committee
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The proposed meeting between the Joint Parliamentary Committee on 'One Nation, One Election' and Supreme Court judges will not take place, sources said.
The Committee had earlier proposed to meet the Chief Justice of India and Supreme Court Judges on October 6 for "informal discussions" on simultaneous elections.
However, the Supreme Court has declined the proposal of the Committee, according to sources.

Earlier in the day, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal, in a press conference, had criticised the Committee's move to meet the Supreme Court judges by saying that it was a violation of the separation of powers.
Sibal stated that such a meeting had never happened in the history of the country.

The Joint Parliamentary Committee is examining the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, which seek to facilitate simultaneous elections.

The committee, headed by BJP MP P.P. Chaudhary, has been conducting consultations with political parties, legislators, constitutional experts and other stakeholders as part of its examination of the two Bills.

The committee has previously stated that it has also consulted former Chief Justices of India, former Supreme Court judges and other legal experts on the constitutional implications of simultaneous elections.

stories.headline: Alleged clash during bank election: CPI(M) leaders get bail
stories.title: Alleged clash during bank election: CPI(M) leaders get bail
stories.summary: M. Girish and C.P. Jaleel were arrested in a case registered over a clash that occurred around two-and-a-half years ago on the day of the Chevayur Cooperative Bank election
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Kozhikode Principal Sessions Court has granted bail to Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] district secretariat member M. Girish and Elathur branch committee member C.P. Jaleel in a case registered in connection with a clash reported on the day of the Chevayur Cooperative Bank election.
Mr. Girish and Mr. Jaleel were arrested last month in connection with the case, which included charges related to an alleged attempt to cause death.
The case originated from a complaint filed by a Congress leader.
The CPI(M) had alleged that the case against its members was false and politically motivated.

The party leaders who accorded a reception to the two near the Kozhikode jail claimed that an earlier police inquiry had found no factual basis for allegations arising from an incident that occurred around two-and-a-half years ago.
Meanwhile, the Congress leaders had alleged that several of their workers were attacked during the clash.
They had also alleged that there was inordinate delay in arresting the suspects.

stories.headline: S.I.R Controversy: Election Commission Drops Extra Form 6 Declaration After Internal Objections
stories.title: S.I.R Controversy: Election Commission Drops Extra Form 6 Declaration After Internal Objections
stories.summary: Amid the Opposition’s escalating campaign against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission, the poll panel has removed the additional SIR-linked declaration from online Form 6 in states where the SIR process has been completed. Form 6 is used by new voters to apply for inclusion in the electoral roll. The additional declaration had asked applicants to establish whether they or their parents or grandparents appeared in an earlier electoral roll. Two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had reportedly raised objections to the way the requirement was incorporated into the online process. The change does not apply uniformly: where SIR is still underway, the additional declaration continues during the SIR process. The Election Commission has maintained that the declaration was an additional SIR document rather than a formal amendment to the statutory Form 6.

stories.headline: President Murmu pays tribute to Mahatma Gandhi on eve of his 157th birth anniversary
stories.title: President Murmu pays tribute to Mahatma Gandhi on eve of his 157th birth anniversary
stories.summary: New Delhi [India], October 1 : On the eve of Mahatma Gandhi's 157th birth anniversary, President Droupadi Murmu paid tribute to him, saying his message of peace and non-violence holds vital relevance amid ongoing global conflicts. “On behalf of all citizens, I pay my respectful tribute to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, on his 157th birth anniversary, celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti,” the President said in her message on the eve of Gandhi Jayanti. According to the release, Murmu said Gandhi’s life and ideals are widely respected by the global community and noted that an atmosphere of war and conflict prevails in many parts of the world, affecting all nations. “In these circumstances, Mahatma Gandhi’s message of peace and non-violence becomes even more relevant,” she said. The President said India is advancing towards the national goal of becoming Viksit Bharat by 2047, with priority being given to the values of empathy and inclusion to ensure that no citizen is deprived of the benefits of development. She said this vision reflects the spirit of Mahatma Gandhi’s ideal of ‘Sarvodaya’, based on the principle of the welfare and upliftment of all. “On the auspicious occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, let us reaffirm our commitment to building an empowered, developed and Atmanirbhar Bharat through our ethical conduct and active participation,” Murmu said. Meanwhile, Union Minister for Coal and Mines G Kishan Reddy called for a nationwide 30-day cleanliness drive from Gandhi Jayanti on October 2 to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary on October 31, urging citizens, government and private institutions, educational establishments, NGOs and other organisations to participate. Speaking to the media, Reddy said the cleanliness campaign should begin from people's homes and workplaces, with government and private offices, educational institutions, NGOs, associations and sanitation workers participating in the drive. "From Gandhi Jayanti to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary, which is coming up on October 31st, for almost 30 days, everyone should take up this Swachh Bharat campaign program across the country, and an appeal has been made for everyone in the country to become participants," Reddy said. (ANI)

stories.headline: Cafe 3 norms: India shifts gears on EVs, opens road for multiple powertrains
stories.title: Cafe 3 norms: India shifts gears on EVs, opens road for multiple powertrains
stories.summary: After nearly 30 months, multiple drafts and a lobbying war that reached the Prime Minister’s Office, India has notified its third set of fuel-efficiency rules for cars that will decide the kind of products carmakers will develop over the coming years.The final Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency, or Cafe, norms come into effect from April next year and seek 16.7 percent better efficiency from new cars by 2032. The government has allowed carmakers to get there by almost any road: Electric vehicles (EVs), range extenders, ethanol, hybrids, or others.Unlike other emission norms such as Bharat Stage, Cafe applies to a carmaker’s entire fleet instead of individual cars.When a carmaker calculates its fleet average, cleaner vehicles are multiplied. Under the final Cafe norms, an EV sold will count as three cars, as will a range extender. Plug-in hybrids and flex-fuel strong hybrids will count as 2.5 cars, strong hybrids as 1.6 and flex-fuel vehicles as 1.1 cars.The first draft from April 2024 that was made public in June had proposed a higher—4 times—benefit for EVs and there was no mention of range extenders. The benefit for hybrids was lower, with plug-ins at 2 and strong hybrids at 1.2. The maximum concession was for hydrogen fuel cell cars at 5, which have disappeared from the final list.The surprise entry is the range extender, or range-extended electric vehicle (REEV), which is practically an EV with a small combustion engine that only works as a generator to charge the battery. No carmaker currently sells REEVs in India but almost all of them are developing this tech. JSW-MG unveiled a platform in July that can be used to develop range extenders while Suzuki talked about it in its latest Technology Strategy briefing.Also Read: In defense of small cars: Why Maruti Suzuki is pushing for less stringent fuel efficiency norms“We are likely to see several range extender launches, as they combine the benefits of electrification with the convenience of longer range and reduced charging concerns,” says Puneet Gupta, director at Mobility Global. opening: After nearly 30 months, multiple drafts and a lobbying war that reached the Prime Minister’s Office, India has notified its third set of fuel-efficiency rules for cars that will decide the kind of products carmakers will develop over the coming years.
The final Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency, or Cafe, norms come into effect from April next year and seek 16.7 percent better efficiency from new cars by 2032.
body: The government has allowed carmakers to get there by almost any road: Electric vehicles (EVs), range extenders, ethanol, hybrids, or others.
Unlike other emission norms such as Bharat Stage, Cafe applies to a carmaker’s entire fleet instead of individual cars.
When a carmaker calculates its fleet average, cleaner vehicles are multiplied.
Under the final Cafe norms, an EV sold will count as three cars, as will a range extender.
Plug-in hybrids and flex-fuel strong hybrids will count as 2.5 cars, strong hybrids as 1.6 and flex-fuel vehicles as 1.1 cars.
The first draft from April 2024 that was made public in June had proposed a higher—4 times—benefit for EVs and there was no mention of range extenders.
The benefit for hybrids was lower, with plug-ins at 2 and strong hybrids at 1.2.
The maximum concession was for hydrogen fuel cell cars at 5, which have disappeared from the final list.
The surprise entry is the range extender, or range-extended electric vehicle (REEV), which is practically an EV with a small combustion engine that only works as a generator to charge the battery.
No carmaker currently sells REEVs in India but almost all of them are developing this tech.
JSW-MG unveiled a platform in July that can be used to develop range extenders while Suzuki talked about it in its latest Technology Strategy briefing.

“We are likely to see several range extender launches, as they combine the benefits of electrification with the convenience of longer range and reduced charging concerns,” says Puneet Gupta, director at Mobility Global.
This makes range extenders particularly attractive for larger vehicles and long-distance driving, he adds.
Cafe norms were first introduced in 2017 and a second iteration came in 2022.
The latest norms come into effect from April 1, 2027, and will run till March 31, 2032.
Amitabh Kant, former CEO of Niti Aayog who helped shape India’s early EV push, calls the norms “a huge missed opportunity”.

“The new Cafe norms are backward looking at worst and status quoist at best,” he wrote on X. “EVs become one option among many, when they should be the destination.” The Cafe regime is shifting the focus from simply increasing EV penetration to optimising the entire powertrain portfolio, says Vivek Sharma, automotive director at GlobalData Plc.

“With BEVs/REEVs, hybrids, flex-fuel, 48V systems and other efficiency technologies offering different routes to compliance, Cafe-III will make powertrain strategy—and the balance between vehicle mix, technology and fleet efficiency—more central than ever to OEM strategy.” For carmakers with predominantly ICE-led portfolios, the framework increases the strategic importance of electrified and alternative-fuel powertrains as part of the overall portfolio mix, according to Som Kapoor, Pratik Shah and Aneesh Ajayan, partners, automotive, EY-Parthenon.

Under the new norms, the government will progressively tighten fleet-average fuel-consumption targets, with the benchmark at 3.996 litres per 100 km in 2027-28, falling to 3.3273 litres per 100 km by 2031-32.
This represents an improvement of about 16.7 percent in fuel efficiency over the five-year period.
The rules also give carmakers more flexibility in emissions compliance.

Rather than calculating it annually, the framework introduces two compliance blocks of three years and two years, allowing companies to offset deficits in one year against surpluses generated in another year within the same period.
Manufacturers also have the option of purchasing credits from the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) at prices ranging from Rs2,500 to Rs4,500 per g/km.
Tata Motors had earlier opposed this; Kant agreed on Wednesday.
“How can [the BEE] sell credits?
A regulator can’t be a player in the market it regulates,” Kant wrote.
Companies that outperform Cafe targets can generate surplus credits and trade them with other carmakers facing a shortfall.
Another way for carmakers to improve their fleet-level compliance is by using renewable and low-carbon fuels.
Before a car’s tailpipe CO2 goes into the fleet average, it is discounted for the renewable share of the fuel it uses.
For diesel cars, the discount will depend on the actual biofuel blending percentage notified by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Carmakers can also deduct 1 g/km each for 12 technologies, capped at 9 g/km.

The list includes start-stop systems, tyre pressure monitoring, regenerative braking, 6-speed or higher transmission, efficient alternators, 12V/48V efficient alternator, 12V/48V motor generator, LED exterior lighting, advanced glass, electric water pumps, high-efficiency air conditioning systems, solar-reflective paint and pulse width modulation-controlled radiator fans.
For the first compliance block—FY28 to FY30—these savings are self-declared by the carmaker.
Only from FY31 must claims be backed by test results generated in accordance with the methodologies and procedures specified by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
The draft norms had divided the auto industry, with the country’s largest carmaker against almost every other large player.
Maruti Suzuki, which makes some of the lightest and most fuel-efficient petrol cars, had asked for higher concessions to be given to small cars, saying compliance costs could finish off this segment.
The September 2025 draft added such a relief.
It said sub-4 metre petrol cars, with engines of up to 1,200 cc and an unladen weight of 909 kg or less, could deduct 3 g/km each from their CO2 figure.
This split the industry, with most carmakers opposing any weight-based relief.
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles MD and CEO Shailesh Chandra had argued that easing rules on the basis of weight could compromise safety.
This relief has been removed from the final norms and the government has instead given a concession to small cars by adjusting the target-setting formula.
The September 2025 draft had used a reference weight of 1,170 kg and a steeper slope.
The final rules move the reference weight to 1,229 kg and flatten the slope.
As a result, the target for a small car, which would have been 54.1 g/km under the September 2025 draft after the relaxation, is now 63.7 g/km without the separate 3 g/km concession.

“The regulation recognises the contribution of multiple powertrain technologies and fuels encouraging multi-faceted R&D and innovation,” says Rahul Bharti, senior executive officer, corporate affairs at Maruti Suzuki.
A credit/debit mechanism is an improvisation over the previous Cafe-II regulation, he adds.
It also sells some strong hybrids, which count as 1.6x, and has entered the EV market with the eVitara though sales are yet to pick up.
Tata Motors built India’s EV market and is the largest electric player even today, a powertrain that gets three times the benefit.
“The continued recognition of zero-emission technologies reinforces the critical role of electrification in achieving India’s long-term decarbonisation objectives,” says Tata Motors’ Chandra.
Mahindra & Mahindra runs one of the heaviest fleets in the country and also has a diesel-heavy portfolio.
Its answer is EVs, a technology it has been investing in through its born-electric platform.

“At Mahindra, we are confident in our ability to meet these norms, backed by our sustained investments in technology, electrification and cleaner mobility,” says Velusamy R, president, automotive business, M&M.Hyundai India is betting on a mix.

Vikram Gulati, country head of Toyota Kirloskar Motor, the champion of strong hybrids in India, says the regulation is a big step forward and will play an important role in India’s march towards realising its goal of energy independence by 2047 as well as carbon net-neutral by 2070.
Smaller players selling fewer than 1,000 cars a year are exempt from the targets, but must report their fleet averages to the BEE.
Shenu Agarwal, president of auto industry body Siam, calls the targets “aggressive” and welcomes the “market-based compliance mechanism”.
JSW Motors, the Sajjan Jindal-led company that will likely launch its first car this year, is a clean-fuel carmaker and will have no issues with compliance.
CEO Ranjan Nayak says, “JSW Motors particularly welcomes the higher volume derogation factor of 3.0 for BEVs and REEVs, followed by 2.5 for PHEVs/eligible strong hybrids.

This appropriately recognises the greater contribution of battery-led technologies while allowing other electrified powertrains to play a role in the transition.” For component makers, a multi-fuel rulebook means more work across more platforms.
The industry is moving towards greater powertrain diversity rather than a sudden replacement of one technology with another, says Suresh D, group chief technology officer at Spark Minda.
He says suppliers must build capability in power electronics, battery management, vehicle control and electrical systems, while still serving conventional engines.
“Given that Cafe III is a fleet-level requirement, the industry will need solutions that can be scaled across multiple vehicle platforms rather than being restricted to a single model or powertrain.”

Automobile sales have grown at a healthy pace across rural and urban markets, underscoring the breadth of consumption”.Also Read: GST Collections Hit 5-Month High of Rs2.04 Lakh Crore in SeptemberStrong start to the yearReal GDP grew 7.8 percent in Q1 FY27, the highest first-quarter growth in the current series, while real GVA expanded 8.2 percent. The major increase in area coverage has been reported in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh Reservoir storage is 70.29 percent of capacity, and groundwater remains largely stable as on September 3.Also Read: In numbers: How El Niño weighs on India's monsoonsGlobal headwindsThe report warns that global conditions have turned “unfavourable”. Oil prices spiked in September and global bond yields are climbing sharply. A lower risk premium on Indian debt is pressuring the rupee. reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 1) stayed the Karnataka High Court's directions constituting a Special Investigation Team (SIT) and ordering a de novo investigation into alleged irregularities in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) Veterinary Officer recruitment scam.

A bench of Justice Manoj Misra and Justice Vijay Bishnoi passed the interim order while hearing the Karnataka government's challenge to the September 21 judgment of the High Court, which had constituted an SIT to investigate alleged irregularities in the recruitment of 400 Veterinary.
Officers and related allegations concerning other KPSC recruitments.
The Court issued notice returnable on October 12 and directed the State to file an additional affidavit in a sealed cover setting out its objections, if any, to the officers appointed to the SIT.
The State may also suggest alternative names for the team.
The interim stay applies to paragraphs 34(i) and 34(ii) of the High Court's judgment, which provide for the constitution of the SIT and a de novo investigation into the alleged crimes.
“In the meantime, the directions in paragraph 34(i) and 34(ii) shall remain stayed.
Issue notice returnable on 12th October.
By the next date, the state shall submit in sealed cover delineating the objections, if any, against the members of the SIT constituted under the order of the High Court.
They may also suggest alternative names for the SIT”, the Court ordered.
During the hearing today, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal for the State argued that the Crime Investigation Department (CID) was already investigating the cases and the probe was nearing completion.
He submitted that there were no specific allegations against the CID officers investigating the present cases to warrant a fresh investigation.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks AG To Consider Plea To Enhance State Bar Councils' Strength
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks AG To Consider Plea To Enhance State Bar Councils' Strength
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(October 1) requested the Attorney General, R. Venkataramani, to consider the plea of increasing the statutory limit of the State Bar Councils, which at present stands at 25 members as per Section 3(2)(b) of the Advocates Act, 1961.

A bench comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed an order while hearing a writ petition filed by one advocate, who has contended that the statutory restriction of SBCs to 25 members was kept at a time when the 1961 Act was enacted.
But over time, the electorate has grown substantially.
For instance, he pointed out that the Bar Council of Delhi presently comprises 2 lakh registered advocates, which necessarily requires adequate and proportionate representation in the elected body.

The present writ petition, filed through AoR Nikhi Jain, has been preferred by one Rohit Pandey, who contested this year's Bar Council of Delhi Elections and secured 2,259 votes but fell short of 63.5 votes to be included among the 25 members of the SBC.

However, because of the Supreme Court's direction reserving 30% representation for women advocates in the SBCs, a low-ranking woman candidate was declared elected even though she secured only 265 votes.
As per his plea, the declaration of the said woman candidate as an elected member is contrary to the 1961 Act.
Supplementing this, Senior Advocate Vikas Singh and other senior advocates contended that Article 142 can't be used to pass a judicial order which is contrary to the statutory scheme.
Considering the brief submissions, the Court deemed it fit to pass a similar order it had passed on September 2.
Justice Bagchi, while passing the order, said: "We are absolutely aware of the judicial limitation, and that's why requesting the Attorney General."
The Court orally stated that if the AG takes a contrary view, the Court will consider.

On September 2, the Court, while hearing another writ petition on enhancement of seats in Bar Councils of Maharashtra and Goa, stated that the issue involves taking a policy decision and therefore requested the AG to treat the writ petition as a representation and take appropriate decisions in consultation with the SBCs.
